ML_Evolution.inherited: From SwarmIntelligence_Swarm_Intelligence_Algorithms: Machine learning begins by asking what changes across generations. Carry this distinction with you: inherited traits, environmental rewards and the rules that keep an experiment running all shape what can survive.
ML_Evolution.question: Can a population change without a single specimen being named the best?
ML_Evolution.ontology: Variation and reproduction can change a population without an explicit ranked fitness score. Survival still depends on implemented resources and constraints.
ML_Evolution.experiment: Follow a few different bodies in the small field, then compare the population, birth and death counts over time.
ML_Evolution.observe: Bodies wander, expend energy, gain energy in previously unvisited cells, reproduce above an energy threshold, and die at zeroenergy.
ML_Evolution.limit: No ranked objective does not mean no selection pressure. Energy for novelty, decay and populationcaps favour some behaviour over others.
ML_Evolution.variation: Existing: watch persistence without choosing a champion. Proposed: expose the exploration reward and compare which bodies persist; curator uniform/culled modes are illustrations, not evolved results.
ML_Evolution.handoff: The gradient landscape next puts an objective in full view. Instead of inheriting a reward through survival, a moving point will be told exactly how its position is scored.
open_questions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Try the written encounter in the actual museum, alone and with a group. Check visibility, reach, the stated response and the handoff before accepting a room baseline.

ML_Gradient_Landscape.inherited: From ML_Evolution: The gradient landscape next puts an objective in full view. Instead of inheriting a reward through survival, a moving point will be told exactly how its position is scored.
ML_Gradient_Landscape.question: Will the same observations lead to the same best fit when error is measured differently?
ML_Gradient_Landscape.ontology: A loss assigns a number to modelparameters. Here each terrain is a function of slope w and intercept b for the same small dataset.
ML_Gradient_Landscape.experiment: Watch the three balls descend their labelled terrains. Change Outliers, then watch where each path travels; use the reset button for another run.
ML_Gradient_Landscape.observe: MSE, Huber and the third oscillating loss produce different surfaces and paths. The Outliers knob regenerates the data and restarts balls at the same parameterpair.
ML_Gradient_Landscape.limit: A minimum is relative to the chosen penalty and model. The artifact label adversarial names a custom wavyloss, not GAN training or adversarial robustness.
ML_Gradient_Landscape.variation: Existing: add outliers and ask which deviations each loss discounts or magnifies. Proposed: mark whose observations become outliers instead of treating that designation as selfevident.
ML_Gradient_Landscape.handoff: The classification room will exchange a fitted line for groups. The same question remains: which differences does the chosen measure treat as important?
open_questions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

ML_Classification.inherited: From ML_Gradient_Landscape: The classification room will exchange a fitted line for groups. The same question remains: which differences does the chosen measure treat as important?
ML_Classification.question: When points share a colour, has a group been discovered or assigned?
ML_Classification.ontology: K-means alternates nearest-centroid assignment with moving each centroid to its assigned points mean; k is chosen in advance.
ML_Classification.experiment: Choose one point near the boundary between colours. Watch its assignment and the neighbouring centroid move through automatic iterations.
ML_Classification.observe: Centroids move and point colours can change. Motion stops when totalcentroid movement falls below the threshold or50iterations are reached.
ML_Classification.limit: This is unsupervisedclustering, not supervisedclassification. Colours do not name natural or ethical categories. The displayed totaldistance sums ordinary distances although textbook k-means minimizes squared distances.
ML_Classification.variation: Existing: compare a peripheralpoint to a centralpoint. Proposed: expose k or curate ring/braid cohorts to ask whether the mean-and-distance rule preserves the grouping the visitor sees.
ML_Classification.handoff: The neural-network room introduces learned connections between layers. It will still need an account of what its training examples and error measure ask it to preserve.

ML_Neural_Networks.inherited: From ML_Classification: The neural-network room introduces learned connections between layers. It will still need an account of what its training examples and error measure ask it to preserve.
ML_Neural_Networks.question: What changes in a network when its answers become closer to the examples?
ML_Neural_Networks.ontology: A neuron computes an activation from weightedinputs plusbias. Backpropagation distributes outputerror into parameterupdates across layers.
ML_Neural_Networks.experiment: Follow one connection while watching the epoch/error display during automatic training. Compare its appearance early and later; also inspect the direction from inputs tooutputs.
ML_Neural_Networks.observe: Weighted links and activations change as actual batches update weights/biases; the error history records the batcherror, which need not decrease on every step.
ML_Neural_Networks.limit: Fitting four examples cannot establish generalintelligence or out-of-distribution reliability. A visible network diagram omits the choice of examples and targetlabels.
ML_Neural_Networks.variation: Existing: track a connection that changes sign or strength. Proposed: compare heldout inputs or a curator topology change while retaining the same examples.
ML_Neural_Networks.handoff: Perception next asks what enters such a model. Before a network can learn from an image, some distinctions must already be made available as input.
open_questions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

ML_Perception.inherited: From ML_Neural_Networks: Perception next asks what enters such a model. Before a network can learn from an image, some distinctions must already be made available as input.
ML_Perception.question: Which parts of this display were computed from pixels, and which were supplied as names?
ML_Perception.ontology: A local filter combines pixelvalues to produce a featuremap. Objectclassification is a separate inference from that numericaloperation.
ML_Perception.experiment: Compare the input cross/circle to its edgeimage. Follow the moving3×3window, then inspect the objectboxes and percentages.
ML_Perception.observe: Broad bright interiors give way to edge responses at changes. The window tours locations; the named detectionboxes are also visible, but their percentages are fixed labels.
ML_Perception.limit: A confidentcaption is not a measurement. A real localedge computation does not automatically justify the objectnames next toit.
ML_Perception.variation: Existing: point out an imagefeature that contributes to anedge yet has no namedbox. Proposed: visitor pixelpainting wired to the existing setter, or curator invented boxes on unchangeddata.
ML_Perception.handoff: The sequence-memory room adds another source of evidence: what happened before the current input arrived.
open_questions: Sobel filtering is computed, but object names and confidence values are supplied in advance. Connect a recogniser to changing input and show evidence for its decisions.
Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

ML_Sequence_Memory.inherited: From ML_Perception: The sequence-memory room adds another source of evidence: what happened before the current input arrived.
ML_Sequence_Memory.question: What would a memory need to keep, admit and reveal separately?
ML_Sequence_Memory.ontology: An LSTM distinguishes persistent cellstate, newinput and output; gates weight retention, writing and reading. This room provides a spatialdiagram of those roles.
ML_Sequence_Memory.experiment: Locate FORGET, INPUT and OUTPUT spheres and follow the particlepath through thecell. Compare the roles before reading their names as a memoryalgorithm.
ML_Sequence_Memory.observe: A stream crosses thecell and gateobjects change visualintensity with activation. The current stream continues independently of the gateactivations.
ML_Sequence_Memory.limit: A moving memorymetaphor does not demonstrate retaining a sequence. Gateobjects are RigidBody3D with collisionlayers; successful museum grabbing has not beenestablished.
ML_Sequence_Memory.variation: Proposed nextbuild: expose a shorttoken sequence, a numericcellstate and gatecontrols that causally alter it; compare preserving an inconvenient input with forgetting it.
ML_Sequence_Memory.handoff: Generative learning next changes the task again: a model produces candidates, while another source of feedback judges them.
open_questions: The gates do not yet control a computed recurrent state. Add a short input sequence, a visible cell state and a two-sequence retention comparison.
Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

ML_Generative.inherited: From ML_Sequence_Memory: Generative learning next changes the task again: a model produces candidates, while another source of feedback judges them.
ML_Generative.question: Who judges a generated example, and how could that judgement change its maker?
ML_Generative.ontology: A generator proposes samples and a discriminator judges samples relative to trainingdata. Their coupled objectives make a feedbackloop; this artifact diagrams itsroles.
ML_Generative.experiment: Move your viewpoint between generator and discriminator, then trace the labelled feedbackroute and compare the two displayedlosses.
ML_Generative.observe: Separatezones, samplemarks, a feedbackloop and a competitionpillar animate. Generatorloss falls and discriminatorloss oscillates in thedisplay.
ML_Generative.limit: The diagram can locate the roles but cannot establish that samples improve, that judging works or that the system reached equilibrium. Similarappearance is not evidence of training.
ML_Generative.variation: Proposed: a small realdataset, generatedsample and discriminator score linked by anactual update; allow visitor disagreement with the selected examples ofrealness.
ML_Generative.handoff: The synthesis room looks directly at that outside: how does a model decide that an observation is an anomaly?
open_questions: The displayed losses are timed curves. Add a small actual generator/discriminator update with visible samples before using falling losses as evidence of learning.
Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Do not claim visitor judging/noisethrowing trains aGAN. Thismap needs a causalexperiment beyond diagram coverage.

ML_Synthesis.inherited: From ML_Generative: The synthesis room looks directly at that outside: how does a model decide that an observation is an anomaly?
ML_Synthesis.question: Is a point unusual by itself, or unusual under a particular measuringrule?
ML_Synthesis.ontology: An anomaly score measures departure from a reference; a threshold turns that score into a decision.
ML_Synthesis.experiment: Find one raised highlightedpoint and one unraisedpoint. Compare their positions to the maincloud and read the displayed mode/threshold.
ML_Synthesis.observe: Points meeting the active threshold rise.25units and scale1.35; the summary counts flaggedpoints. Default mode is Z-score and threshold2.4.
ML_Synthesis.limit: Flagging is a relation to thisdataset and chosenrule, not proof that an event or person iswrong. Other named modes are heuristics; autoencoder_error is a handwritten sinusoidalresidual, not a trainedautoencoder.
ML_Synthesis.variation: Proposed: wire existing mode/threshold APIs into visitorcontrols and retain the samepoint while its designation changes. Untilthen compare the visiblepoint positions in the defaultmode.
ML_Synthesis.handoff: Graph theory will give us another representation of relations. Instead of asking how far points lie from a centre, we will ask which points are connected and what those connections permit.
open_questions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
No VRcontrol is wired for mode/threshold; do not instruct knob use.
